title: Dunsmuir on I-5: Exits, Food, Gas and Stops
meta: Dunsmuir sits at exit 729 on I-5, with listed gas, food and lodging at nearby exits plus Castle Crags and Hedge Creek Falls close by.
intro: Dunsmuir is a railroad town in the canyon on I-5, with Castle Crags' granite spires rising west of the freeway. This page lists the nearby exits and the gas, EV, food and lodging mapped around them, plus landmarks worth a stop. Services come from OpenStreetMap and are not live.

faq.q: What exit is Dunsmuir on I-5?
faq.a: Dunsmuir is at exit 729 (I 5 Business; Dunsmuir). Exit 730 (Central Dunsmuir) and exit 732 (Siskiyou Avenue, Dunsmuir Avenue) also serve the town.

faq.q: Where is gas in Dunsmuir off I-5?
faq.a: Gas is mapped at two exits: a Valero at exit 729 and a Chevron at exit 730. A ChargePoint EV charger is also mapped at exit 730. These are listed in the data, not live, so check before you rely on them.

faq.q: Where can I eat in Dunsmuir near I-5?
faq.a: Exit 730 (Central Dunsmuir) has the most food mapped, with seven places including Burger Barn, Cafe Maddalena and Pizza Factory. Exit 732 lists Penny's Diner and Sten's Burger Strand, and exit 728 lists the Jubilee Railroad Dining Car.

faq.q: Where can I stay in Dunsmuir off I-5?
faq.a: Exit 732 has the most lodging mapped, with eight listings including Cedar Lodge Motel and Travelodge. Exit 728 lists Jubilee Railroad Wilderness Lodge, where a lodge founded in 1968 lets guests sleep in old cabooses.

faq.q: What is there to see in Dunsmuir on I-5?
faq.a: Castle Crags is at exit 726, on the left going north. A short trail from exit 732 leads to Hedge Creek Falls, where you can walk behind the falling water, and Upper Soda Springs is a riverside park under the freeway at exit 730.
